title: Get started with Consensus MCP
snippet:
MCP is the fastest way to give an assistant or agent paper search. Owkin plugged Consensus MCP into its agentic AI scientist and went from curated PubMed abstracts to 25x the paper coverage in days. Browse the use cases.
**Server URL**
```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

**One-click:** open [Consensus in the Claude directory](https://claude.ai/directory/65247229-f0c7-49df-9044-fcbb8b3894c6) and click **Connect**. Or connect manually:
1
Open Settings
Open [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) or the Claude desktop app and go to **Settings**.
2
Browse connectors
Select **Connectors**, then **Browse connectors**.
3
Find Consensus
Search for **Consensus** and click **Connect**.
4
Sign in
Approve the sign-in with your Consensus account, or continue without one at reduced limits.
5
Start searching
Ask a research question in any chat. Consensus appears in the tools menu.
```
claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

Or add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:
```
[mcp_servers.consensus]
url = "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
```
**One-click:** [Install in Cursor](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=consensus&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL21jcC5jb25zZW5zdXMuYXBwL21jcCJ9). Or add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"consensus": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "mcp-remote@latest", "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"]
}
}
}
```
Add to your MCP configuration:
```
{
"servers": {
"consensus": {
"url": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Add to your MCP configuration:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"consensus": {
"serverUrl": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
}
}
}
```

But to use the MCP, click ‘model context protocol’.

title: Use Consensus in ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or with the API
snippet:
Connect another tool
Using a different assistant or tool, such as Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code? Connect it to the Consensus MCP server directly. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants to use outside tools. The server is hosted, so there’s nothing to install:
```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```
##
​
What your assistant can do
**Search.** The `search` tool returns ranked papers with title, authors, journal, publication year, citation count, study type, a key takeaway, and a link to the paper on Consensus. On paid plans it also returns query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers, so your assistant can quote the passage behind each claim. Your assistant can pass the same filters Research Agent uses:
- Year range, study type, and journal quartile (SJR)
- Human and controlled studies, minimum sample size, minimum citations
- Medical mode, open access only, exclude preprints
- Study duration and country

Supported clients
Claude (web, desktop, and Claude Code), ChatGPT and ChatGPT Deep Research, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, and any client that supports remote MCP servers.

Use the API
Building your own tool, agent, or workflow? The Consensus API gives you the same paper search over REST, and can run Research Agent as a Thread. Send a query, get back ranked peer-reviewed papers with metadata, and skip running each search by hand. It’s self-serve and open to everyone.
```
GET https://api.consensus.app/v1/search
```
- The top 20 most relevant papers per query by default; raise `page_size` for more, up to your plan’s maximum
- Metadata on every paper: title, authors, journal, year, DOI, citation count, and a link
- On paid plans: study design, journal rank, key takeaways, and query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers
- The same filters as the web app: publication date, study type, sample size, citations, journal quality, field, country, and open access

title: GitHub - Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp: Official Consensus MCP server. Semantic search over 400M+ research papers, including all of PubMed, for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any MCP client.
snippet:
The official Consensus MCP server gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Perplexity and any other MCP client semantic search over **400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers and all of PubMed**. Your assistant can find research papers, filter them by study design and journal quality, and give answers that cite real studies, without leaving the chat.
It's a hosted remote server, so there's nothing to install. Connect, ask a research question, and get back ranked papers with DOIs, citation counts, study type, sample size and a one-line takeaway.
**Server URL**
```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

### Claude (web and desktop)
One click: open [Consensus in the Claude directory](https://claude.ai/directory/65247229-f0c7-49df-9044-fcbb8b3894c6) and click **Connect**. Or manually:
1. Open [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) (or the Claude desktop app) and go to **Settings**
2. Select **Connectors**, then **Browse connectors**
3. Search for **Consensus** and click **Connect**
4. Approve the sign-in with your Consensus account (or continue without one at reduced limits)
5. Ask a research question in any chat; Consensus appears in the tools menu

Any client that supports remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP) works. Point it at `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp` and sign in with OAuth, or send an API key as a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

There are good MCP servers for PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar, most of them open-source wrappers around a free metadata API. Consensus works differently:
- **Coverage.** One server covers all of PubMed plus the rest of science (400M+ articles), so you don't need a separate server per database.
- **Ranking.** Search is semantic and tuned for research questions, rather than a pass-through to a keyword or Boolean API.
- **Evidence signals on every result.** Study type, sample size, journal quartile and a plain-language takeaway come back with each paper, so the assistant can weigh evidence instead of just listing it.
- **Full text.** Licensed and open-access full text, not abstracts only.
- **Hosted and supported.** A remote server with OAuth, API keys, SSO and SOC 2, maintained by the Consensus team. Nothing to self-host.

Building your own application, RAG pipeline or agent? The same search is available as a REST API at `api.consensus.app/v1/search`, with a Threads API for the research agent. See the [consensus-api](https://github.com/Consensus-NLP/co

title: Getting Started with the Consensus MCP
snippet:
The Consensus MCP server enables AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and other MCP-compatible clients to search over 200 million peer-reviewed academic research papers directly from the conversation.
##
Getting Started
Consensus MCP lets AI assistants search 200+ million peer-reviewed research papers. Connect your preferred client below — you'll be searching in under 2 minutes.
> **Server URL:**`https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`
>
> The `/mcp` path is required. Using `https://mcp.consensus.app` alone will not work.

Cursor
Add via **Settings → Tools & MCP → New MCP Server**, or edit your config directly:
```
{ "mcpServers": { "Consensus": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "mcp-remote@latest", "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" ] } } }
```

Security
- **Endpoint:** Only connect to the official URL: `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`
- **API keys:** Store securely using environment variables. Never share keys in prompts or public conversations. Rotate if compromised.
- **Data handling:** Search queries are sent to the Consensus API over HTTPS/TLS. Results contain publicly available academic paper metadata. No personal data is stored from MCP requests.
---
##
Supported Platforms
| Platform | Auth | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Desktop | OAuth | Supported |
| ChatGPT | OAuth | Supported |
| ChatGPT Deep Research | OAuth | Supported |
| Claude Code | OAuth | Supported |
| Codex | OAuth | Supported |
| Cursor | OAuth | Supported |
| VS Code (GitHub Copilot) | Config | Supported |
| Windsurf | Config | Supported |
| Other MCP Clients | Bearer token | Supported |

title: consensus.tools | Decision Firewall for AI Agents
snippet:
# MCP Server
Model Context Protocol server that exposes consensus-tools as tools, resources, and prompts for LLM agents.
## Overview
`@consensus-tools/mcp` is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives Claude Code or any MCP-compatible client access to the full consensus-tools stack. It registers 31 tools across six areas, plus resources and prompts for guided interactions. Consensus tools use `snake_case`; the rest use dotted names.
## Installation
```
pnpm add @consensus-tools/mcp
```
## Quick start
### Claude Code integration
Add to your `.claude/settings.local.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"consensus-tools": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["@consensus-tools/mcp"]
}
}
}
```
With environment configuration:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"consensus-tools": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["@consensus-tools/mcp"],
"env": {
"CONSENSUS_STORAGE_PATH": "/path/to/state.json",
"CONSENSUS_AGENT_ID": "my-agent"
}
}
}
}
```
ℹ
Zero config by default
Without any environment variables, the MCP server stores state at `~/.local/share/consensus-tools/state.json` and uses `mcp-agent` as the default agent identity. Every tool except `audit.explain` works with zero external dependencies.
## Environment variables
| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CONSENSUS_STORAGE_PATH` | `~/.local/share/consensus-tools/state.json` | Path to the JSON state file |
| `CONSENSUS_AGENT_ID` | `mcp-agent` | Agent identity for consensus operations |
## MCP tools (31 total)
The standalone server (via `npx @consensus-tools/mcp`) registers 31 tools across six areas.

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `guard.evaluate` | Evaluate any action against guard policies. Requires an explicit `action.type` the server has an evaluator for (the built-in domains, plus any custom evaluators registered on the engine) |
| `guard.send_email` | Evaluate an outbound email — flags secrets/credentials and risky attachments |
| `guard.code_merge` | Evaluate a PR/merge — flags auth/security/crypto file changes, failing tests, and vulnerability patterns in the diff |
| `guard.publish` | Evaluate content before publishing — detects profanity and PII (e.g. SSN) |
| `guard.support_reply` | Evaluate a support reply — escalates refund commitments and legal threats |
| `guard.agent_action` | Evaluate a generic agent action — blocks unapproved irreversible actions |
| `guard.deployment` | Evaluate a deployment — flags production deploys for review |
